background.title: A living Filipino martial art
background.body: Arnis, also known by names including Eskrima and Kali, is a Filipino martial art with traditions of weapon-based and empty-hand practice. Its forms and teaching methods vary across regions and schools. This short introduction is a draft for classroom use and should be reviewed by a Filipino Arnis instructor.
steps: Learn the name and local tradition taught by your instructor.
Practice only with approved training equipment and supervision.
Show respect for training partners and the cultural roots of the art.

background.title: Arnis as a Filipino martial art
background.body: Arnis is recognized as a Filipino martial art and national sport. Training can include coordination, discipline, safe partner practice, and respect. Activities in this app are introductory learning materials, not a substitute for supervised instruction.
steps: Listen to your teacher's safety briefing.
Use the stance and movement taught in your class.
Stop immediately when a teacher or partner calls for a pause.

background.title: Why learn Basic Arnis?
background.body: Basic Arnis lessons give students a structured way to practice movement, balance, coordination, focus, and safe cooperation. Skills should be learned progressively, with age-appropriate equipment and teacher supervision.
steps: Warm up before practice.
Keep safe spacing from other students.
Reflect on one skill to improve after each lesson.

fundamentals.title: Proper grip
fundamentals.body: Hold the approved training stick firmly but without unnecessary tension. Keep the thumb wrapped safely and follow the exact grip demonstrated by your teacher. Never point a stick at a person.
steps: Use only an instructor-approved training stick.
Wrap the fingers around the handle without squeezing hard.
Keep the stick controlled and pointed away from people.
fundamentals.image_placeholder: Close-up grip demonstration pending instructor review.

fundamentals.title: Ready position
fundamentals.body: The ready position is the balanced starting posture your teacher uses for a lesson or sequence. Keep your gaze forward and maintain enough space to move safely.
steps: Stand in the stance shown by your instructor.
Keep knees relaxed and weight balanced.
Hold the training stick in the taught safe position.
fundamentals.image_placeholder: Front and side ready-position reference pending.

fundamentals.title: Basic stances
fundamentals.body: Stances create a stable base for movement. Your teacher may demonstrate ready, forward, or other class-specific positions. Do not force a deep stance if it causes pain.
steps: Place your feet as demonstrated.
Keep your balance centered and knees comfortable.
Hold still briefly, then return safely to ready position.
fundamentals.image_placeholder: Ready and forward stance reference images pending.

fundamentals.title: Basic strikes
fundamentals.body: Basic strikes are taught as controlled movement patterns. Practice slowly in an open area, using only the target and direction approved by your teacher.
steps: Begin in the taught ready position.
Move through the strike path at a controlled speed.
Return to a balanced final position without striking a person.
fundamentals.image_placeholder: Strike phase images pending teacher validation.

fundamentals.title: Basic blocks
fundamentals.body: Blocks are defensive movement patterns practiced with safe spacing and supervision. Use the direction and target taught in class; never test a block on another student.
steps: Start from ready position.
Move into the taught block path with control.
Recover to a balanced position and wait for the next instruction.
fundamentals.image_placeholder: Block demonstration images pending instructor review.

fundamentals.title: Footwork
fundamentals.body: Footwork includes controlled forward, backward, side, and triangle steps. Keep movements small enough to maintain balance and avoid collisions.
steps: Check that the practice area is clear.
Move one step at a time in the direction taught.
Regain balance before beginning another movement.

fundamentals.title: Body coordination
fundamentals.body: Coordination brings stance, footwork, and upper-body movement together. Learn each part slowly before practicing a complete sequence.
steps: Practice the stance on its own.
Add one footwork pattern at a slow pace.
Combine the movements only when your teacher says it is safe.
